claims.text: Atomic layer deposition of platinum-group metals on high-surface-area supports improves catalytic activity relative to conventional catalyst synthesis.
Atomic layer deposition of platinum-group metals on high-surface-area supports improves catalyst durability relative to conventional catalyst synthesis.
Atomic layer deposition reduces platinum-group-metal consumption relative to conventional catalyst synthesis.
A high-surface-area support serves as the structural mediator of the intervention.
Atomic layer deposition increases platinum-group-metal dispersion.
Atomic layer deposition increases utilization of platinum-group metals.
The intervention will improve catalytic activity by 20% relative to conventional catalyst synthesis.
The intervention will improve durability by 15% relative to conventional catalyst synthesis.
The intervention will reduce platinum-group-metal consumption by 30% relative to conventional catalyst synthesis.
The predicted effects should hold from 500 to 900 degrees Celsius at space velocities of 50,000 to 100,000 h^-1.
Failure to achieve at least 10% higher activity, 10% higher durability, and 20% lower platinum-group-metal consumption would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted improvements are 20% activity, 15% durability, and 30% consumption reduction, but the falsification rule accepts substantially smaller improvements of 10%, 10%, and 20%. Results between those values would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the proposed rule.
